newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corporate new issue mart in late summer lull.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corporate new issue mart in late summer lull.

text.p: Pre-holiday doldrums, higher U.S. Treasury yields and light staffing are all expected to dampen the pace of corporate bond issuance this week, dealers said.

"I've been trying to scour around and see if anything's going on, but I've been hardpressed to find anything. Unless there's a significant market move things are going to be very quiet," one syndicate source said.

The Public Securities Association has recommended an early 1400 EDT/1800 GMT close for the U.S. Treasury market on Friday, ahead of Monday's Labor Day holiday when U.S. financial markets will be closed.
Meanwhile, Friday's backup in U.S. Treasury yields should keep issuers sidelined for now as financing costs have now been driven higher, dealers said.
An unexpectedly strong July durable goods report on Friday caused a sharp selloff in the Treasury market.

The U.S. Treasury's sale of $18.75 billion in two-year notes on Tuesday, and another $12.5 billion in five-year notes on Wednesday, should serve to hamper any further potential corporate debt issuance.
"It's very quiet. This week's Treasury auctions will keep potential issuers at bay," said another syndicate source.
In the meantime, amid late summer doldrums players were seen squabbling over days off and the last chance for an extended holiday weekend at the shore as the summer comes to a close, dealers said.
"The market is expected to remain in a lull up until the next batch of (U.S.) employment data," one dealer said.
The U.S. Labor Department will release its next report on the labor sector on Friday, September 6.
